title: Factor an injective fs chart through free generators and a group-isomorphism chart
statement:
Let $P,Q$ be fine saturated commutative monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and let $g:P\to Q$ be a homomorphism for which $g^{\rm gp}:P^{\rm gp}\to Q^{\rm gp}$ is injective. Suppose its cokernel $L=Q^{\rm gp}/g^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})$ is torsion free, meaning $n\ell=0$, $n>0$, implies $\ell=0$. Then there exist an integer $r\geq0$ and elements $q_1,\ldots,q_r\in Q$ whose images form a $\mathbf Z$-basis of $L$. In particular the homomorphism
$$h:P\oplus\mathbf N^r\longrightarrow Q,\qquad (p,(n_i))\longmapsto g(p)+\sum_i n_iq_i$$
is injective and $h^{\rm gp}:P^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z^r\to Q^{\rm gp}$ is an isomorphism. The direct sum here is the Cartesian product with componentwise addition, and a $\mathbf Z$-basis means that every element has a unique expression as an integer linear combination. The empty basis is allowed when $r=0$.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71, the injective monoid chart with free cokernel; Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.2 and 3.1.9--3.1.10, printed pp. 98--99, for sharpening, localization and finite saturated monoids. The free-generator factorization is an agent-supplied algebraic refinement; its argument is recorded in report.md, not attributed verbatim to ILO.

proof.text: Put $G=Q^{\rm gp}$, $H=g^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})$, $L=G/H$, $\pi:G\to L$, and $S=\pi(Q)$. By [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $P,Q$ embed in their completions. Finite monoid generators of $Q$ generate $S$ and generate $L$ as a group, since elements of $G$ are differences from $Q$. Thus [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] and the torsion-free hypothesis identify $L$ with $\mathbf Z^r$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75, finite basis for a finitely generated torsion-free group; agent-supplied application to the cokernel of the chart of VI 1.9.

proof.text: The monoid $S$ is root saturated in $L$: suppose $n\ell\in S$ with $n\geq1$ and $\ell\in L$. Lift $\ell$ to $x\in G$ and choose $q\in Q$ with $\pi(q)=n\ell$. Since $nx-q\in H=g^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})$ and every element of $P^{\rm gp}$ is a difference of elements of $P$, there exist $a,b\in P$ with $nx=q+g(a)-g(b)$. Then $n(x+g(b))=q+g(a)+(n-1)g(b)\in Q$, using $n-1\geq0$. Saturation of $Q$ in $G$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives $x+g(b)\in Q$, whose image is $\pi(x)=\ell$; hence $\ell\in S$. No face hypothesis on $g(P)$ and no torsion-freeness of $G$ is used.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, printed p. 101, saturation convention; explicit quotient-image calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: If $r=0$, take the empty basis. Otherwise [lem-trf-lattice-monoid-minimal-determinant-tuple] gives columns $v_i\in S$ with least positive $D=|\det A|$. By [lem-trf-integer-matrix-fractional-lattice-witness] they are rationally independent; if their integer span were proper, choose $y$ outside it and apply that node to obtain $x=Aa\in\mathbf Z^r$ with $0\leq a_i<1$ and $a_j>0$. By [lem-trf-saturated-monoid-fractional-column-descent], replacing column $j$ by $x$ gives columns in $S$ and determinant strictly between $0$ and $D$, a contradiction.

source.place: Assembly of the three agent-supplied lattice lemmas: old steps 3--6; Tag 0F0K (algebra-item-cauchy-binet), Tag 07DQ (algebra-lemma-matrix-left-inverse, adjugate identity).

proof.text: Hence the $v_i$ span $L$ over $\mathbf Z$ and are independent, so integer coordinates in them are unique. Lift each $v_i$ to $q_i\in Q$ using $S=\pi(Q)$; in rank zero no choices are needed.

source.place: Agent-supplied basis-lifting refinement of the injective chart with free cokernel in VI Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71.

proof.text: Define $\Phi(u,m)=g^{\rm gp}(u)+\sum_i m_iq_i$. If $\Phi(u,m)=0$, applying $\pi$ gives $m=0$ by the basis, then $u=0$ by injectivity of $g^{\rm gp}$. For $t\in G$, write $\pi(t)=\sum_i m_iv_i$; then $t-\sum_i m_iq_i\in H$ equals $g^{\rm gp}(u)$ for some $u$. Thus $\Phi:P^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z^r\to G$ is an isomorphism, also for $r=0$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71, free-cokernel chart; explicit group calculation supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Restrict $\Phi$ to $P\oplus\mathbf N^r$: nonnegative coefficients give values in $Q$, and this is $h$, with $h(p,0)=g(p)$. Equality of $h$-values gives equality under $\Phi$, hence equality of the inputs, since $P\hookrightarrow P^{\rm gp}$ and $Q\hookrightarrow Q^{\rm gp}$ are injective [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], as is $\mathbf N^r\hookrightarrow\mathbf Z^r$. Finally a homomorphism $P\oplus\mathbf N^r\to B$ to any abelian group is uniquely the sum of its restriction to $P$ and the images of the coordinate generators. The former extends uniquely to $P^{\rm gp}$; the latter extend by integer multiples. This proves $(P\oplus\mathbf N^r)^{\rm gp}=P^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z^r$, under which $h^{\rm gp}=\Phi$.

source.place: VI 1.9 and VIII 3.1.1, group completions; the product universal property is checked directly.
